concept.body: Composite surface bills ONLY exposed faces. Prices: cylinder wall 2πrh (unrolled rectangle), sphere 4πr², hemisphere dome 2πr². At any glued seam the shared circle is interior — counted zero times — while hollows EXPOSE extra faces (a tube shows outer wall, inner wall, and two end rings). Cite the prism surface rules from Grade 6 for the flat-sided pieces.

widget.prompt: A mini-silo: radius 2, wall height 5, hemispherical roof, circular floor. Surface coefficient (of π) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 36 bills the seam circle (4) — interior faces are free: 32.
28 forgets the floor — it stands on a 4π disk: 32.

steps.body: Surface needs two new prices and one discipline. Prices: a sphere's surface is **4πr²** (so a hemisphere's curved dome is 2πr²), and a cylinder's curved wall is its unrolled rectangle: **2πrh**. Discipline: at a seam, the shared circle is INTERIOR — count it zero times. Surface bills only what's exposed.

explanationVariants: The wall unrolls into a rectangle: circumference by height.

widget.prompt: The silo's cylindrical wall (radius 6, height 10) has lateral surface coefficient (of π) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 360 is the VOLUME's coefficient — the wall is circumference × height: 2(6)(10) = 120.
60 forgets the 2 — the unrolled width is the FULL circumference 2πr: 120.
72 prices the dome (2r²) — the wall is 2rh = 120.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 2πrh = 120π — the rectangle the wall becomes when unrolled.

explanationVariants: Exposed: wall 120π + dome 2π(36) = 72π + floor 36π. The JOINT circle: buried.

widget.prompt: Total exposed surface of the silo (radius 6, wall height 10, hemispherical roof, circular floor). Coefficient of π = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 264 bills the joint circle (36) — where dome meets wall is INTERIOR: 120 + 72 + 36 = 228.
300 roofs with a full sphere (144) — the dome shows only 2πr² = 72: 228.
192 forgets the floor — the silo stands on a 36π disk: 228.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 120 + 72 + 36 = 228 — the seam circle appears in NO term.

explanationVariants: Four exposed faces: outer wall 2π(5)(6), inner wall 2π(2)(6), and TWO end rings π(25 − 4) each.

widget.prompt: The tube (outer 5, inner 2, length 6), open at both ends. Total surface coefficient (of π) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 84 counts only the two curved walls — the two end RINGS add 21 each: 126.
105 counts one ring — both ends are exposed: 126.
134 prices the end rings as full disks (25 each) — they're rings of 21: 126.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 60 + 24 + 2(21) = 126 — (equal to its volume coefficient by pure coincidence of these numbers).

widget.prompt: Two solids are glued along a shared full circle. In the composite's surface total, that circle's area is counted:

options.label: Zero times — the seam is interior on both sides; only exposed surface bills
options.feedback: Each piece ALONE would count it once (silo cylinder's top, hemisphere's flat face) — gluing buries both copies.

options.label: Once — it belongs to one piece
options.feedback: It belonged to BOTH before gluing — and to neither after: interior, zero.

options.label: Twice — once per piece
options.feedback: That double-counts a face nobody can touch — zero.

options.label: Depends on which piece is larger
options.feedback: Size is irrelevant — sealed is sealed: zero.

widget.prompt: A sphere of radius 4: surface coefficient (of π) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 16 = 4² forgets the 4 — the sphere's surface is 4πr²: 64.
85.33 ≈ (4/3)(64) is the VOLUME's coefficient — surface is 4r² = 64.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 4(16) = 64 — four great circles' worth, the sphere's famous price.

hints: Exposed: the cylinder wall + two hemispherical domes = wall + one full sphere's surface.
The two seam circles: zero times each.
explanationVariants: 48 + 36 = 84 — and no flat faces anywhere: the capsule is all curve.

widget.prompt: The capsule (cylinder radius 3, height 8, hemispherical caps both ends). Total surface coefficient (of π) = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 102 adds the two seam circles (9 each) — seams are interior: 48 + 36 = 84.
66 caps with one hemisphere (18) — both ends together show a full sphere's 36: 84.
120 doubles the caps (72) — two DOMES of 2πr² = 18 each total 36: 84.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 48 + 36 = 84 — two half-skins make one sphere's worth, over an unrolled wall.

takeaways: New prices: sphere 4πr² (dome 2πr²), cylinder wall 2πrh (an unrolled rectangle).
Seam circles count ZERO times — interior faces never bill.
Hollows expose extra faces: tubes bill outer + inner walls + end rings.
steps.teaser: Final chapter: what scaling does to length, surface, and volume — k, k², k³.
